title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck localizes the presheaf category A^ (A a small category) at the weak equivalences W_A. W_A is induced from the basic localizer W of (Cat), so Hot_A = W_A^{-1} A^. He claims that W_A admits a calculus of fractions. The top line of this page specifies that the morphisms live in \overline{A^}, which most plausibly means the category A^ divided by the homotopy relation. On that reading the claim is a calculus of left fractions in the homotopy-quotient category.

This page treats the cancellation axiom. Given X' --s--> X ⇉(f,g) Y in \overline{A^} with s in \overline{W}_A and fs = gs, is there t: Y -> Y' in \overline{W}_A with tf = tg?
- 'OPS s mono' means 'on peut supposer s mono'. This uses the factorization (i) below.
- fs = gs in the homotopy category gives a homotopy h: I×X' -> Y from fs to gs.
- He forms the double mapping cylinder M as the pushout of I×X' <- X'⊔X' -> X⊔X. M maps to Y by (f,g) on X⊔X and by h on I×X'.
- By (iv), s⊔s: X'⊔X' -> X⊔X is a mono and a weak equivalence. By the gluing condition (ii), I×X' -> M is a weak equivalence.
- By 2-out-of-3, using I×X' -> I×X in W since I is aspheric, the canonical map M -> I×X is in W_A.
- He then pushes out M -> I×X along M -> Y (the dashed arrow I×X ⇢ Y'). This gives t: Y -> Y', with t in W by (ii). The composite I×X -> Y' is a homotopy from tf to tg, so tf = tg in \overline{A^}.

He then isolates the abstract axioms such an argument needs in a pair (M,W) with a class 𝓜 of morphisms (cofibrations, here monomorphisms):
- (i) every map factors as an 𝓜-map followed by a weak equivalence (a 'homotopisme').
- (ii) in a cocartesian square whose top map i is in 𝓜 and whose left map is in W, the pushed-out map is in W. This is a gluing / left-properness axiom.
- (iii) there exist generating families of intervals I_α such that X⊔X -> X×I_α is in 𝓜 for all X. Hence the bottom-left note: these are 'intervalles séparants', i.e. intervals whose two endpoints are disjoint.
- (iv) finite sums behave well, and W is stable under binary coproducts.

The left margin seems to state the general conclusion. In any (M,W) with these properties, W^{-1}M equals \overline{W}^{-1}\overline{M}, the localization of the homotopy-quotient category, with W admitting fractions there. The right margin notes that (i)–(iii) hold in A^ and suffice for W_A.

The next page confirms the plan. A separating interval compatible with W exists in A^ iff I -> e is W_A-aspheric, i.e. iff A is a local test category. Stability of W_A under coproducts is reduced to (Cat) via the localization axiom Loc. 3.

In modern terms this is Brown's / Quillen's theorem that Ho(C) is a localization of the homotopy category πC in which weak equivalences admit a calculus of fractions. It is carried out for presheaves with monomorphisms as cofibrations and a separating interval as cylinder. That is precisely the framework of Cisinski's later model structures on presheaf categories.
errors: As the diagram stands, applying (ii) to the pushout defining Y' needs M -> I×X to lie in 𝓜. This is not justified: M -> I×X is generally not a monomorphism when s is not an iso on endpoints. One must first factor M -> I×X by (i), M -> X_1 -> I×X, and push out M -> X_1 instead. The homotopy tf ~ tg then comes from the generalized cylinder X_1 rather than I×X. This in turn requires that homotopies with respect to such generalized cylinders still identify maps in \overline{A^}. That point is not addressed here.

The step 'fs = gs in \overline{A^} implies a single homotopy I×X' -> Y' is not argued. Homotopy in A^ is the equivalence relation generated by elementary homotopies, possibly via several intervals I_α, so chains of homotopies (zigzags) must be handled.
The argument assumes I×X' -> I×X is in W when s is. This needs I aspheric (I -> e in W after products), which is only made explicit on the next page.

The statement of (ii) as written ('i, f ∈ 𝓜 et f ∈ W, alors g ∈ W') is garbled. The intended statement is: i ∈ 𝓜 and f ∈ W imply that its cobase change g is in W (or the analogous statement with roles swapped).

ideas.what: Calculus of (left) fractions for weak equivalences in the homotopy-quotient category of presheaves, so that Hot_A = \overline{W}_A^{-1}\overline{A^}
ideas.modern_name: Brown's / Quillen's description of the homotopy category: Ho(C) as πC localized with a calculus of fractions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (Homotopical Algebra, 1967); K. S. Brown (1973, categories of fibrant objects); Gabriel–Zisman (1967) for the calculus of fractions
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses modelizers, homotopy relations and localization in presheaf categories; whether this exact fraction argument appears there is unsure

ideas.what: Cancellation via the double mapping cylinder M = I×X' ∪_{X'⊔X'} (X⊔X) and pushout of M -> I×X along M -> Y
ideas.modern_name: Cylinder/gluing argument in a cofibration category (Brown's factorization and gluing lemma)

ideas.what: Abstract axioms (i)–(iv): factorization into 𝓜 followed by a weak equivalence, left properness/gluing along 𝓜, cylinders X⊔X -> X×I_α in 𝓜, stability of W under finite sums
ideas.modern_name: Category of cofibrant objects / cofibration category / left proper structure on presheaves with monos as cofibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brown 1973 (dual), Waldhausen 1985, Baues 1989; for presheaves, Cisinski 2002–2006
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks has related 'modelizing' and 'contractibility structure' discussions

ideas.what: Separating interval required (X⊔X -> X×I a monomorphism); existence of a W_A-compatible separating interval equivalent to A being a local test category (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Separating segment / interval; local test categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, 1983); developed by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (separating intervals, test and local test categories); Maltsiniotis, 'La théorie de l'homotopie de Grothendieck' (Astérisque 301)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches, for an arbitrary basic localizer W on (Cat) and local test category A, axioms making (A^, monos, W_A) a left-proper cofibration category with separating-interval cylinders. He aims to deduce that Hot_A is a localization of the homotopy-quotient category with a calculus of fractions. This anticipates the cofibration/cylinder machinery Cisinski later used to build model structures for arbitrary localizers on presheaves. It is not original, since Brown and Quillen already had the abstract statement, but it documents Grothendieck working in this direction.
missed.quote: (iii) ∃ familles génératrices d'intervalles I_α, telles que pour tout X, X ⊔ X → X × I_α soit ∈ 𝓜 ... ce sont donc des intervalles séparants
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck himself moving toward abstract cofibration axioms on presheaves governed by an arbitrary localizer, the route later systematized by Cisinski.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is essentially Brown/Quillen's calculus of fractions in the homotopy category via mapping cylinders, specialized to presheaves with separating intervals. The link to local test categories is already in Pursuing Stacks and in the Maltsiniotis/Cisinski literature. The value is historical only.
transcription_corrections: Top line: the morphisms are taken 'de \overline{A^}' (bar over A^, the homotopy-quotient category), not plain \hat{A}; likewise s, t ∈ \overline{W}_A.
'OPS s mono' abbreviates 'on peut supposer s mono'.

Diagram: the top-left X' is crossed out. The arrow labelled ∈W_A goes to I×X, which maps by a dashed arrow to Y'. The vertical arrow M -> I×X is labelled [∈W_A], and t: Y ⇢ Y' is dashed. I×X' ↪ M is labelled [∈W_A]. The bold arrow joins X'⊔X' and I×X', and X'⊔X' -> X⊔X is labelled ∈W_A. A diagonal arrow X⊔X -> Y is drawn.
In (i), after 'h homotopisme', there is an inserted word above the line, possibly 'propre', with a struck-through '(I_α)'.
(iv) reads roughly 'Bien sommes finies cartésiennes dans M, et f,g ∈ W ⇒ f⊔g ∈ W'. A struck line beneath mentions coproducts.
Left margin begins 'Dans toute (M,W) ... W^{-1}M = \overline{W}^{-1}\overline{M}', most likely with a bar on M as well, i.e. a statement about the homotopy-quotient category.
Near (ii)/(iii), the vertical note reads approximately 'modifier pour avoir ...'. Bottom-left reads 'ce sont donc des intervalles séparants'.
